title: variantly — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Cupping Table for the local app (wizard, generation board, comparison view). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Cupping Table
options.lineage: specialty-coffee cupping: numbered cups, blind tasting, the printed score form
options.thesis: Every variant is a numbered cup on one table; you taste them blind, mark the form, and keep one.
materials: glazed porcelain rims seen from above
a printed score form ticked in blue ballpoint
options.viewport: Your site fills the screen; along the bottom edge a row of numbered porcelain rims is the 1…N picker, the active cup circled in ballpoint; the before/after divider is a hairline with a spoon-bowl grip.
options.risk: Cupping is niche ritual: if its vocabulary leaks into labels (aroma, crust) it turns into costume instead of a quiet instrument.

raised.raise: Chrome is strictly graphite on porcelain plus one ballpoint blue; the only other colour on screen belongs to the sites being tasted.
Registration: every cup is shown at the same path, scale and scroll ratio, so a difference is always the design, never the framing.
The cup under the spoon lifts; the rest of the row drops to half ink.
Hierarchy by size, not weight: the active cup number is the only large figure in the chrome.

options.label: Better One, or Two?
options.lineage: the optometrist's phoropter and its lens flips
options.thesis: Flip numbered lenses in front of your own site until one is sharp, exactly like the eye exam everybody has sat through.
options.viewport: The site seen through a circular lens bezel; a dial of numbered lenses around the bottom edge; '1 or 2?' is literally the prompt between two variants.
options.risk: The most familiar shape for a compare tool; closest to what A/B tools already look like.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: airport departure boards and the segmented boarding pass
options.thesis: Variants depart like flights: the board reranks live as agents work, and each variant carries a pass with its number and summary.
options.viewport: Generation is a departures board, row per variant with status that holds its alert colour until seen; comparison docks the board to one strip.
options.case: Holds audience identification (everyone reads a gate board) and makes waiting legible; loses on the choosing moment, which it has no native gesture for.
options.risk: Split-flap theatre turns playful fast; the board has to stay an instrument.

options.label: Catalog Numbers
options.lineage: Factory Records sleeves: FAC numbers and colour-coded titles
options.thesis: Every variant is a catalog entry, V01 to V10, its look encoded as a strip of its own colours; only the selected one is decoded.
materials: hue-block code strips sampled from each variant
options.viewport: Matte black around the site, a strict V-number index at the edge with each variant's sampled palette as a code strip.
options.case: Holds product clarity (number-coded variants with their palette as a strip is instantly readable); loses audience identification with most developers.
options.risk: Matte black chrome lands close to the dark dev-tool default.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Variants as poster tiles in a scrolling row.
options.case: Fuses into a thumbnail gallery, which is exactly the screenshot grid variantly exists to replace.
options.kept: The focused item lifts while the rest dim.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Variants as stars ranked by magnitude.
options.case: No ranking exists among variants; magnitude would invent one.
options.kept: Hierarchy carried by size instead of type weight.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Variants as registered plates on one baseline.
options.case: Cream-and-serif lands in the rut and fights the sites being compared.
options.kept: Strict registration: same scale and position for every comparison.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Agent output as strobing barcode fields.
options.case: Strobing fights a decision you make by looking calmly.
options.kept: Total monochrome discipline in the chrome.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern dev-tool app: neutral dark chrome, segmented tabs, a variants sidebar, done at Linear/Vercel craft.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, variant tabs, the site in a framed viewport.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dev tool by design.
